work.summary:
How to run variant 5 yourself through IBKR with IB Gateway, and what it costs. Everything is before tax; there is no tax content. Folder: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-snt-2b-adam-cieniewicz/4246b01c-1857-5934-aed2-b3eb85d88a07/scratchpad/audit/ib_gateway/. build_ib_gateway.py writes 4 CSVs: 56 sourced facts, the budget line items, a per-tier summary and the time estimates. Nothing under /home/user was modified.

1. IB GATEWAY SETUP
- IB Gateway is TWS without the charts. It has the same login and the same API, uses about 40% fewer resources, and is the version pysystemtrade recommends.
- The API is free; you pay only for market data. API orders are charged the normal IBKR Pro commissions. I found no surcharge for using the API, but also no explicit IBKR statement that rates are identical.
- You need an IBKR Pro account. IBKR Lite has no API access at all (error "API support is not available for accounts that support commission free trading"). Lite is also not offered to EEA clients of IBKR Ireland.
- Account fees and access:
  - No inactivity fee since 2021.
  - Extra usernames are free. Create one username only for the Gateway: there is one session per username, so logging in on mobile or TWS would otherwise kick the Gateway off.
  - Market data is billed per username, so subscribe on the API username only.
  - Real-time data requires USD 500 of equity.
- Paper account:
  - Free, same API. Ports: Gateway 4002 paper / 4001 live (TWS 7497/7496).
  - Live subscriptions can be shared with the paper account; otherwise it gets delayed data.
- Hardware: about 4 GB RAM (8 GB recommended). Java is bundled. One loaded instance uses about 1 GB.
- Restarts and 2FA:
  - Use daily Auto Restart (not Auto Log Off). The Gateway then restarts each day without logging in again.
  - Once a week, after 01:00 ET on Sunday, a full login with second factor is required. 2FA is mandatory and is approved with a push on IBKR Mobile.
  - IBC (free) automates start, login, the daily restart and 2FA retries (the alert times out after about 3 minutes). It cannot approve the 2FA for you.
  - IBKR server resets: 00:15–01:45 ET and 06:25–07:45 CET. Schedule jobs outside these windows.
- Docker: the usual image is gnzsnz/ib-gateway-docker (IB Gateway stable 10.50.1e / latest 10.51.1b, IBC 3.24.2, TRADING_MODE paper/live/both, VNC optional). Alternative: QuantConnect IBAutomater.
- Limits:
  - 50 API messages per second (100 default market-data lines ÷ 2).
  - Historical requests: no identical request within 15 s, at most 60 per 10 minutes. Strict limits are now documented only for bars of 30 s or less.
  - None of this binds a 14–40 market daily system.
- Orders: market, limit and IB Adaptive. Adaptive works for US futures via `algoStrategy='Adaptive'` (Urgent/Normal/Patient) and is DAY only. pysystemtrade's default algo (passive limit, then aggressive) needs live streaming data. Use `algoSnapMkt` (market orders) for markets on delayed data.

2. DATA THROUGH THE API
- Free delayed data needs no subscription: `reqMarketDataType(3)`, or 4 for delayed-frozen. Delays: CME/CBOT/NYMEX/COMEX 10 min, ICE US and ICE Europe 10 min, Eurex and Euronext 15 min, OSE 20 min.
- Historical bars are the uncertain point. IBKR's API docs say historical bars always need a Level-1 real-time subscription. pysystemtrade's maintainers write that this stopped being enforced in early 2023, without announcement, "so things may change". Test it on your own username before relying on it.
- Expired futures: bars are available up to 2 years after expiry (`includeExpired`). That is enough to warm up the signals, not to rebuild a long history. To seed history:
  - Carver's free CSVs stop on 2024-03-28 (checked).
  - A community set (bug-or-feature/pst-csv-data) covers 40 instruments to 2025-09-23.
  - Norgate: USD 270/yr; its updater runs only on Windows.
  - Databento: from USD 0.50/GB with a USD 125 free credit. Good for CME; Eurex starts only in 2025.
- Subscriptions (non-professional):

| Subscription | Cost | Note |
|---|---|---|
| US Securities Snapshot & Futures Value Bundle (CME/CBOT/NYMEX/COMEX) | USD 10/month | Waived in any month with ≥ USD 30 commissions |
| Eurex | EUR 2–12/month | Carver pays EUR 8.75 (Eurex Core) + EUR 2 (Eurex Retail Europe); low confidence |
| Euronext Bundle | EUR 3/month | |
| Osaka (OSE) | about JPY 200/month | Possibly not offered to non-professionals; low confidence |
| ICE Futures US | USD 148/month | Exchange's 2026 non-professional rate; exact IBKR price not found |
| ICE Europe commodities | USD 161/month | Same |
| ICE Europe financials | USD 139/month | Same |

- Estimated IBKR commissions are USD 46–66/month at 100k, so the US bundle is free on average (borderline in quiet months). They are USD 108–154 at 250k and USD 335–479 at 1M.
- What can be skipped: all ICE real-time data, and OSE. A daily system can use delayed data plus market or Adaptive orders. The audit's cost model already pays the half-spread, so this is consistent with the simulated costs.
- Exchanges needed by tier:
  - 100k (14 markets): CME group, Eurex, Euronext and OSE.
  - 250k (24) adds ICE US (canola, sugar No. 11) and ICE Europe financials (Euribor, SONIA).
  - 1M (40) adds cotton (ICE US) and white sugar (ICE Europe commodities).

3. PYSYSTEMTRADE
- Repo moved to pst-group in January 2026. It needs Python ≥ 3.10 and MongoDB + Parquet, and switched from ib_insync to ib_async (≥ 2, < 3) in April 2026. ib_async is the maintained fork of ib_insync; its original author died in 2024.
- It connects to the Gateway on 127.0.0.1:4001 with a client id.
- What runs daily:
  - `run_daily_price_updates`: FX, sampled contracts, IB historical bars and back-adjusted prices; it can download by region.
  - `run_capital_update`.
  - `run_systems`: recomputes the backtest to get optimal positions.
  - `run_strategy_order_generator`.
  - `run_stack_handler`: sends orders, records fills and reconciles positions.
  - Reports, backups and cleaners.
- Still needs a human:
  - the weekly 2FA approval;
  - price spikes, which block the data write and send an email asking for a manual check;
  - rolls through `interactive_update_roll_status` (manual, semi-automatic or automatic; passive rolling recommended);
  - broken or missing data, and Gateway upgrades.
- Variant 5's rules (EWMAC, strategy 13 volatility regime, portfolio vol targeting; trend.py is about 200 lines) must be ported as custom rules, or into a lean ib_async script.

4. BUDGET (USD/yr, fixed costs; % of capital)

| Budget | 100k | 250k | 1M |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimal | 134 (0.13%) | 124 (0.05%) | 124 (0.01%) |
| Standard | 412 (0.41%) | 402 (0.16%) | 402 (0.04%) |
| Comfortable | 841 (0.84%) | 4,265 (1.71%) | 6,197 (0.62%) |

- Minimal: Hetzner CX23 (USD 99/yr incl. 20% VAT) or a home PC (about USD 25/yr of electricity), US bundle waived, everything else delayed, free history, FX conversions USD 25. Its weakness: it relies on IB still serving historical bars without a subscription, which is undocumented.
- Standard, recommended as the central case:

| Line | USD/yr |
|---|---|
| Hetzner CX33, 8 GB | 148 |
| US bundle (one missed waiver month at 100k) | 0–10 |
| Eurex | 148 |
| Euronext | 41 |
| OSE | 15 |
| ICE | 0 (delayed data + market orders) |
| FX conversions | 50 |

- Comfortable: a second VPS for paper trading or backup, Norgate at USD 270, FX USD 100, and ICE real-time where markets are held (USD 3,444 at 250k, USD 5,376 at 1M). ICE real-time is not worth it at any tier up to 1M.
- Full running cost per tier, standard budget:

| Cost (% of capital per year) | 100k | 250k | 1M |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variable: fees + half-spread (audit, verified; ER4 spread corrected; already inside the simulated Sharpes) | 3.30 | 3.65 | 2.87 |
| Fixed | 0.41 | 0.16 | 0.04 |
| Cash interest lost vs €STR (audit) | 0.79 | 0.67 | 0.61 |
| Total | 4.50 | 4.48 | 3.52 |
| Not already inside the simulated Sharpes | 1.20 | 0.83 | 0.65 |

- Keep "Excess Funds Sweep → securities" on, so that only the required margin sits in the futures segment, which earns no interest.
- Note: the sibling before-tax simulations assume USD 150/yr of fixed costs. The standard budget adds about 0.26% per year at 100k and is negligible at 1M.

5. TIME AND STEP-BY-STEP PLAN
- Setup: about 80–200 h for 14–40 markets if you are fluent in Python (the audit's 200–500 h was for all 84).
  - Account: 3–8 h.
  - VPS and Docker: 4–12 h.
  - pysystemtrade configuration: 15–40 h.
  - Porting the rules: 30–100 h.
  - Seeding history and reconciling: 15–40 h.
  - Then 8–12 weeks of paper trading at 1–2 h/week.
- Recurring: about 1–2 h/week on average.
  - The 2FA tap: about 2 min/week, but you must be reachable.
  - The daily report: 5–10 min.
  - Rolls: 62 / 106 / 169 roll orders a year, i.e. 5–15 h/yr.
  - Monthly checks: 1–2 h.
  - Yearly review and upgrades: 10–20 h.
- Plan:
  1. Open IBKR Pro (Ireland), request futures permissions, and check that every contract is tradeable (it needs a KID). Create the API username and the paper account; share data with the paper account.
  2. On a Hetzner CX33: Ubuntu, Docker, ib-gateway-docker with IBC in paper mode. Ports bound to localhost, VNC only through an SSH tunnel, AutoRestart, relogin after a 2FA timeout.
  3. Install pysystemtrade and MongoDB, configure the subset, seed history, port variant 5, and reconcile positions against the backtest.
  4. Paper-trade 2–3 months, covering rolls, restarts, the Sunday 2FA and a Gateway upgrade.
  5. Go live with part of the capital (e.g. CME markets or about 1/3), then scale up.

Main uncertainties:
- Whether historical bars keep working without a subscription.
- Exact IBKR prices for Eurex, OSE and ICE.
- Whether the commission waiver is met every month at 100k.

In time.csv, the 30–100 h for porting the rules and the 80–200 h total are my own estimates, not sourced.

verification.summary:
I checked the ib_gateway job's claims against sources I fetched myself (raw GitHub re-downloaded on 5 Oct 2026), new web searches and a recomputation from the simulation CSVs. Most of the job holds. Every budget total reproduces exactly, and so do the variable costs (3.30/3.65/2.87 %) and the cash shortfall (0.79/0.67/0.61 %). Corrections the report must make:

(1) Hetzner CX servers. Since about 2–7 Sep 2026, every Hetzner CX/CAX plan (the cheap tier) is marked unavailable, and stock comes and goes. The fallback CPX plans cost 3–4 times more: CPX32 is about $593/yr. Write the server line as "any 8 GB VPS at about €7–11/month incl. VAT, so $99–148/yr" (OVH VPS-1 and netcup are examples), not as a guaranteed CX33.

(2) ICE real-time prices. USD 148/161/139 are AMP's non-professional rates from 1 Jun 2026. ICE's own 2026 schedule lists $132 (ICE US) and $123 (ICE Europe financials). Use a range of 123–161 per feed. I could not find the exact IBKR price.

(3) IBKR commission estimate. Mapping each market to its IBKR rate gives an IBKR share of only about 25–36 % of the simulated all-in fee, because most contracts are micros where exchange fees dominate. Monthly commissions are therefore about $33–66 at 100k (central ~$42). The $30 waiver for the US bundle is met on average but is borderline at 100k, so budget $10–60/yr for that line at 100k.

(4) Historical data without a subscription. The newer IBKR TWS API docs say delayed data can be used with reqHistoricalData. Together with pysystemtrade's note that a subscription stopped being required in early 2023, this means the minimal and standard budgets are less fragile than the job says. It still needs testing. Also, pysystemtrade's IB updater fetches only about 1 year of daily prices. Carver's CSVs (end 2024-03-28) cannot be bridged from IB. The community set (end 2025-09-23, 40 instruments, no Schatz/Euribor/SONIA/canola/sugar/cotton) is now just past that window. The plan should seed history from the user's own backtest data.

(5) Eurex. Eurex Retail Europe covers only equity-index micro/mini futures. Schatz and Bobl need Eurex L1/Core, about EUR 8–8.75/month. So the Eurex line is $110–148/yr; keep 148 as the upper bound.

(6) OSE. An IBKR Japan fee guideline lists Osaka L1 as fee-waived for non-professionals (it may not apply to IBKR Ireland clients); Carver (a UK client) pays JPY 200. The line is $0–15/yr.

(7) IB Adaptive. It works on futures on US and non-US exchanges, single-leg orders only, DAY only — not only US futures.

(8) Before-tax simulations. They do not "assume USD 150/yr". cv_avant_impot runs $150, $400 and $1,000, and the report-ready table uses $400 as the central case. That matches the standard budget (402–412). The comfortable budgets at 250k and 1M ($3.9–6.2k) exceed even the $1,000 sensitivity.

(9) Optional robust standard budget. Adding Norgate ($270) at 250k and 1M as a fallback for ICE daily closes gives $672 (0.27 % / 0.07 %). The total running cost then becomes 4.59 % and 3.55 %.

(10) Home PC. The $25/yr electricity figure assumes a 12 W mini-PC. A desktop costs about $60–120/yr.

Also confirmed: 2FA is per username and IB Key can hold several usernames on one phone; paper logins need no 2FA (secondary source); there is also a Saturday reset (00:00–02:00 ET); gnzsnz maps container ports 4003/4004 to host 4001/4002.

Time estimates are the author's own and unverifiable. No tax content is used anywhere.

checked.claim: Estimated IBKR commissions USD 46-66/month at 100k, 108-154 at 250k, 335-479 at 1M (35-50% of all-in fees); US bundle free on average
checked.correct_value: 100k: about USD 33-66/month (central ~42); 250k: 85-154; 1M: 275-479. IBKR share is about 25-36% of the simulated all-in fee. The waiver is met on average at every tier but borderline at 100k; budget USD 10-60/yr for the bundle at 100k.
checked.evidence: Per-market IBKR rates (micro US 0.25, E-micro FX ~0.15, std US 0.85, Eurex EUR 0.90 = $1.03) against fee_spec in simulation/contracts_small.csv. Fee base = (fee+half-spread − half-spread) × capital = $1,582 / $3,710 / $11,460 per yr; 1,470 / 3,234 / 10,395 contract sides per yr.

checked.claim: Eurex EUR 2-12/month; Carver pays Eurex Core 8.75 + Retail Europe 2
checked.correct_value: Eurex Retail Europe covers equity-index micro/mini futures only, not fixed income. Schatz (100k tier) and Bobl (1M) need Eurex L1/Core, about EUR 8-8.75/month, plus 0-2 for Retail Europe: EUR 8-10.75/month = USD 110-148/yr. Keep 148 as the upper bound.
checked.evidence: pst production.md table (raw): Eurex Core EUR 8.75, Retail Europe EUR 2 (2021 prices). IBKR via search: Eurex L1 non-pro EUR 8, L2 EUR 12. Deutsche Boerse Eurex Retail Europe product sheet: micro ESTX50/DAX/SMI, Mini-DAX, STOXX 600, sector, options, vol, FX; no fixed income listed.

checked.claim: Euronext Bundle EUR 3/month
checked.evidence: IBKR market-data pricing (search snippet): Euronext Bundle L1 non-pro EUR 3.00. Some sources show EUR 2-5. Medium confidence.

checked.claim: Osaka (OSE) about JPY 200/month, possibly not offered to non-professionals
checked.correct_value: JPY 0-200/month (USD 0-15/yr). IBKR Japan's fee guideline lists Osaka Top of Book as fee-waived for non-professionals; Carver (UK client) lists JPY 200. Whether it is offered to IBKR Ireland clients is unconfirmed.
checked.evidence: interactivebrokers.com/download/ibsj/EN-Fees_Disclosures.pdf (via search); pst production.md.

checked.claim: ICE non-pro real-time 2026: ICE US USD 148, ICE Europe commodities 161, ICE Europe financials 139 per month
checked.correct_value: These are AMP's pass-through rates (effective 1 Jun 2026). ICE's own 2026 schedule: ICE US Ags & Financials USD 132, ICE Europe Financials USD 123 per ID per month (ICE US rises to 140 in 2027). Use a range of 123-161 per feed; the exact IBKR price is unverifiable.
checked.evidence: ampfutures.com/trading-info/exchange-data-fees and ice.com/publicdocs/data/Market_Data_Subscriber_Fees.pdf (both via search snippets; direct fetch blocked).

checked.claim: Sibling before-tax simulations assume USD 150/yr fixed costs; standard budget adds ~0.26%/yr at 100k
